name: Basal cell skin cancer
theme: the commonest cancer · the rarest killer

meta.title: Basal cell carcinoma in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Basal cell carcinoma of the skin (localized, locally advanced, and metastatic), adult
meta.population: Adults with basal cell carcinoma - THE COMMONEST CANCER AND THE RAREST KILLER: millions of US cases yearly (the commonest human cancer) yet metastasis occurs in 0.0028-0.55% of cases (verified range; the ~0.1% point estimate memory-grade) and death is extraordinarily rare - AND the denominator is honestly unknowable because SEER excludes nonmelanoma skin cancer (the same registry-exclusion honesty as the AL amyloidosis trainer). The router is the NCCN risk stratification (secondhand, guideline-grade): high-risk features (location in the H-zone of the face, size, ill-defined borders, aggressive histologic subtype, recurrence, immunosuppression, perineural invasion) route to margin-controlled surgery; low-risk disease opens a genuinely plural menu where the livelier research question is DE-ESCALATION. The advanced chapter is tiny and real: hedgehog-pathway inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) and cemiplimab after them. THE SURVIVAL TIE is the spec's teaching centerpiece: survival cannot rank this menu - every local door shares one number because BCC almost never kills - so the real currency is RECURRENCE, carried on the cards at its verified grade but never ranked.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the commonest cancer and the rarest killer. THE SURVIVAL TIE anchors the local chapters: every local-therapy door carries the same survival number (property-enforced) because BCC-specific survival approaches 100% on every road - survival CANNOT rank this menu, recurrence can, and the recurrence receipts are carried at their true grades: the Dutch randomized trial of Mohs vs standard excision (10-year paper PMID-verified) puts 10-year recurrence at 4.4% vs 12.2% - FOR PRIMARY high-risk facial BCC (the sweep CORRECTED the briefing's attachment of these n…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: NCCN BCC risk stratification: high-risk vs low-risk by location/size (H-zone), borders, primary vs recurrent, immunosuppression, prior RT, histologic subtype (morpheaform/infiltrative/micronodular aggressive; nodular/superficial not), perineural invasion - SECONDHAND, guideline-grade (no single PMID; none fabricated); the Mohs appropriate-use criteria (270 scenarios) PMID-verified as the operational companion
meta.response: The currency of this disease is RECURRENCE, not survival: 10-year recurrence 4.4% after Mohs vs 12.2% after standard excision for PRIMARY high-risk facial BCC (verified snippet - and the entity discipline matters: the briefing mis-attached these numbers to recurrent disease; the sweep corrected it - the stack's FIFTH premise correction; the trial's recurrent-BCC-arm numbers were not captured and are NOT stated); advanced disease uses ORR (labeled endpoints - displayed, never ranked)

Newly diagnosed.name: Mohs micrographic surgery (high-risk local - the margin-controlled standard)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the high-risk-local standard (NCCN secondhand; AUC verified)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized 10-year recurrence receipt (verified, primary facial BCC) + verified AUC
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: local surgery - the trade is time in the chair for margin certainty
Newly diagnosed.patient: For higher-risk spots - especially on the face: the specialized surgery that checks all the margins the same day, with the lowest chance of the spot ever returning.

Newly diagnosed.name: Standard excision, 4mm margins (low-risk local - the workhorse)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the low-risk workhorse (NCCN secondhand; margin receipt verified)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a simple office procedure and a scar
Newly diagnosed.patient: For low-risk spots: a straightforward office excision with a small safety margin - the everyday cure for the everyday cancer.

Newly diagnosed.name: The topical/destructive toolbox (low-risk local - plural by evidence)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: guideline-listed options for low-risk superficial/nodular disease (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized-with-honesty (SINS verified: inferior to surgery, still usable) + secondhand PDT receipt
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: topical inflammation for the creams; a wound that heals by design for the destructive tools
Newly diagnosed.patient: For small, thin, low-risk spots: creams, light-based treatment, or scraping - real options with one honest caveat: in the head-to-head trial, the cream cured fewer spots than surgery did.

Newly diagnosed.name: Definitive radiotherapy (the non-surgical candidate's road)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: local skin reaction; late cosmetic change - the trade against surgery
Newly diagnosed.patient: For people who cannot or prefer not to have surgery: a course of radiation cures most spots - with one absolute exception taught here: people with the rare inherited Gorlin syndrome should not receive it.

Newly diagnosed.name: Hedgehog inhibitor, locally advanced (vismodegib / sonidegib)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the locally-advanced standard (NCCN secondhand; approvals dated)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: single-arm phase 2 receipts (ORR verified at update-paper grade); survival figure flagged teaching estimate
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cramps, dysgeusia, alopecia - the discontinuation drivers; teratogenic
Newly diagnosed.patient: For basal cell carcinomas too advanced for surgery or radiation: a daily pill that switches off the growth pathway this cancer runs on - it shrinks roughly half of advanced tumors.

Newly diagnosed.name: Hedgehog inhibitor first, metastatic (the rarest chapter)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: single-arm phase 2 receipts (verified at update grade); median flagged teaching estimate
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the very rare situation where this cancer has spread: the daily growth-pathway pill first - it works in a meaningful fraction - with an immunotherapy waiting behind it.
drugs: Vismodegib (preferred metastatic ORR receipt) or sonidegib

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.patient: Comfort-focused care is a real choice - here it mostly means expert wound care and keeping the area comfortable.

refs.label: NCCN Basal Cell Skin Cancer guideline: the high-risk vs low-risk stratification (H-zone location, size by zone, borders, primary vs recurrent, immunosuppression, prior RT, aggressive histologic subtype, perineural invasion) - SECONDHAND, guideline-grade: no single PMID exists for the stratification and NONE IS FABRICATED; NCI PDQ skin cancer page secondhand beside it

The Dutch randomized trial, Mohs vs standard excision for facial BCC: 10-year paper (van Loo, Eur J Cancer 2014 - PMID 25262378, pubmed-url-match): 10-yr recurrence 4.4% MMS vs 12.2% SE - FOR PRIMARY high-risk facial BCC (THE ENTITY DISCIPLINE: the briefing mis-attached these to recurrent disease; sweep-corrected - the stack's FIFTH premise correction; recurrent-arm numbers NOT captured, NOT stated). 5-yr predecessor Mosterd, Lancet Oncol 2008 (PMID 19010733, matched; the van Loo / Mosterd author pair is a documented confusable); earliest report 15541449

AAD/ACMS/ASDSA/ASMS 2012 appropriate use criteria for Mohs micrographic surgery (Connolly, JAAD 2012 - PMID 22959232, pubmed-url-match): 270 scenarios - the operational companion to the risk router; recurrent BCC sits squarely in the appropriate zone

Wolf and Zitelli, surgical margins for basal cell carcinoma (Arch Dermatol 1987 - PMID 3813602, pubmed-url-match): 4mm clears well-demarcated small BCC (117 cases, 2mm increments). THE CONFUSABLE PAIR documented, with an author-swap layer the skin-scc sweep CORRECTED: the companion SCC-margins paper is BRODLAND and Zitelli 1992 (PMID 1430364) - shared senior author, DIFFERENT first author - the next trainer's receipt, not this one

SINS randomized trial, surgical excision vs imiquimod 5% for nodular and superficial BCC (Bath-Hextall, Lancet Oncol 2014 - PMID 24332516, pubmed-url-match): imiquimod INFERIOR to surgery - and still a usable option for small low-risk lesions (the honesty carried on the toolbox card). THE NEAR-TITLE TRAP documented: the SINS protocol paper is PMID 20409337 (Trials 2010) - same trial, different paper

The toolbox's other tools: PDT for superficial BCC - the US Phase 3 composite-clearance receipt (65.5% vs 4.8% placebo, NCT03573401) SECONDHAND; the Ameluz sNDA FILED 2025-11-28 - the FDA decision is a LIVE 2026 watch item (would be the first US-labeled PDT for superficial BCC); curettage-electrodesiccation at its conventional grade (no anchor claimed); 5-FU topical conventional

ERIVANCE vismodegib in advanced BCC: PRIMARY paper (Sekulic, NEJM 2012;366:2171-9, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1113713) - its PMID RESISTED MATCHING across three queries: FLAGGED, cited by journal/DOI (THE ADJACENT-PMID TRAP documented: PMID 22670904 is the NEJM Gorlin-prevention paper by Tang, one integer away - do not conflate). The verified chain: 12-month update PMID 25981002 (J Am Acad Dermatol 2015;72(6), abstract re-read firsthand 2026-09-10 - by independent review the objective response rate INCREASED with the extra follow-up, from 42.9% to 47.6% in locally advanced disease and from 30.3% to 33.3% in metastatic disease, median duration of response in locally advanced disease from 7.6 to 9.5 months, no new safety signals. The figures previously shown, '43% locally advanced / 30% metastatic', are the PRIMARY-analysis numbers carried under the 12-month-update citation, and the 'investigator-assessed 60%/45%' pair appears nowhere in that abstract and has been dropped); final update PMID 28511673 (matched). FDA approval Jan 2012 (secondhand, dated)

BOLT sonidegib in advanced BCC (Migden, Lancet Oncol 2015 - PMID 25981810, pubmed-url-match): ORR at the approved 200 mg dose, by central review, abstract re-read firsthand 2026-09-10: 43% (18 of 42, 95% CI 28-59) in locally advanced disease and 15% (2 of 13, 2-45) in metastatic disease, with 36% (20 of 55, 24-50) in the primary efficacy analysis population; the 200 mg dose had fewer dose interruptions or reductions (32% vs 60%) and fewer serious adverse events (14% vs 30%) than 800 mg. The previously displayed '57.6% locally advanced, 7.7% metastatic' appears nowhere in this publication and has been replaced; long-term updates matched (30-month 28846163; 42-month 31545507). FDA approval Jul 2015, 200mg (secondhand, dated). The la-vs-met asymmetry between the two hedgehog drugs is carried honestly

Cemiplimab after hedgehog inhibitors (Stratigos, Lancet Oncol 2021;22:848-857, DOI 10.1016/S1470-2045(21)00126-1): the PRIMARY PMID RESISTED MATCHING - FLAGGED, cited by journal/DOI; THE FABRICATED-PMID TRAP documented: a summarizer offered 'PMID 34000246' which was NOT in any returned link list - REJECTED. ORR ~31% locally advanced cohort (memory-grade, flagged). REGULATORY: accelerated approval Feb 2021 (secondhand); CONVERTED TO FULL FDA APPROVAL ~Jul 2025 (metastatic, post-hedgehog or hedgehog-inappropriate) - conversion date NOT pinned, flagged for verification against the FDA notice
refs.src: Lancet Oncol (PMID flagged) + FDA conversion (secondhand, date flagged)

refs.label: The hedgehog-pathway receipts (matched): PTCH1 as the Gorlin gene - Johnson, Science 1996 (PMID 8658145, pubmed-url-match); somatic PTCH mutations in sporadic BCC (PMID 9205058, matched; the companion Hahn Cell 1996 PMID did NOT surface - not asserted); vismodegib reduces new BCCs in Gorlin - Tang, NEJM 2012 (PMID 22670904, matched - the same paper that sits one integer from the flagged ERIVANCE primary)

THE EMPTY GORLIN BUCKET (a landscape finding, not a search failure): patidegib gel phase 3 (NCT03703310) COMPLETED AND MISSED its primary (topline 2021; extension closed); sirolimus-gel phase 2b CODY (NCT04893486) COMPLETED 2024-08 and FAILED its new-BCC-prevention primary (nominal lesion-size secondary only) - NO open US Gorlin trial exists and NO successor announced. The 2025 Gorlin guideline (JAAD - secondhand): no recommendation on topical hedgehog inhibitors, 'limited evidence'; the RT-AVOIDANCE rule (RT induces field BCCs in Gorlin) guideline/memory-grade, flagged; germline PTCH1 verified (8658145)

THE RAREST KILLER receipts: von Domarus and Stevens, metastatic BCC - 5 cases + 170 literature review (JAAD 1984 - PMID 6736323, pubmed-url-match): metastasis frequency 0.0028-0.55% (snippet-verified range; the ~0.1% point estimate memory-grade, source-marked). THE DENOMINATOR HONESTY: SEER excludes nonmelanoma skin cancer - the commonest human cancer is registry-uncounted (the AL-amyloidosis exclusion honesty, again); the millions-of-cases epi is memory-grade, consistent, unanchored

ONTRAC phase 3 randomized trial of nicotinamide for skin-cancer chemoprevention (Chen, NEJM 2015 - PMID 26488693, pubmed-url-match): reduced new nonmelanoma skin cancers and actinic keratoses in high-risk patients (~23% relative NMSC reduction at 12 months - memory-grade for the exact figure, flagged)

THE SUNSCREEN HONESTY - Nambour randomized trial (Green, Lancet 1999 - PMID 10475183, pubmed-url-match; 'Green' is the author's surname - a documented summarizer confusion): daily sunscreen prevented SCC; BCC was NOT significantly reduced over 4.5 years - the asymmetric prevention receipt said as found; prolonged follow-up (SCC-specific) PMID 17132769 (matched)

THE TRANSPLANT MULTIPLIER, RE-HOMED by the skin-scc sweep: the multiplier magnitudes (BCC ~10-16x; SCC 65-250x - the next trainer's number) belong to the Euvrard NEJM 2003 review 'Skin cancers after organ transplantation' (PMID 12711744, pubmed-url-match), magnitudes memory-grade; PMID 20410852 (pubmed-url-match) is the subsequent-keratinocyte-carcinoma cohort receipt - a related but DIFFERENT claim, previously mis-attributed here

Definitive radiotherapy for BCC: the non-surgical-candidate road - SERIES-GRADE WITH NO ANCHOR CAPTURED THIS SWEEP (an honest absence, said; no PMID fabricated); NCCN lists it secondhand; the VISORB periocular-vismodegib follow-up (residual histologic disease after clinical response) informs neoadjuvant-HHI caution at secondhand grade

THE SHELF, dated, with TWO LOUD STATUS CONFLICTS: (1) neoadjuvant cemiplimab in resectable head/neck BCC (NCT05929664) - a registry-derived snippet says SUSPENDED ('fianlimab not currently available') while ASCO 2026 abstract 9515 REPORTS RESULTS for its cemiplimab-mono cohort ('acceptable safety, promising efficacy'); best reading (cemiplimab cohort read out; fianlimab portion suspended) UNCONFIRMED - registry re-check REQUIRED before spec use; (2) VA B3C imiquimod-chemoprevention (NCT05212246, 1,630 veterans, 17 centers) - sources conflict between recruiting and not-yet-recruiting. Also watched: the Ameluz sNDA decision (filed 2025-11); ex-US doors NOT listed as US (German first-line cemiplimab NCT06981325; CEMIQUID NCT07251413; pulsed sonidegib+cemiplimab NCT04679480 active-not-recruiting, likely ex-US)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

SP-002 (intralesional adenoviral immunotherapy) + vismodegib in locally advanced BCC (NCT06344052): phase 2, 3-arm randomized open-label (Part A n=20, Part B n=60), Stamford Pharmaceuticals, multicenter US (site list unconfirmed) - RECRUITING, WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-20, registry re-check due. The only recruiting US advanced-BCC interventional door found - NOT a hedgehog-resistant trial (it layers immunotherapy ON vismodegib; no US resistant-specific door exists - said)

Active surveillance for low-risk BCC in elderly patients (NCT06539468, University of Michigan Rogel): the FIRST US prospective AS trial in BCC (low-risk trunk/limb lesions) - RECRUITING, WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-20; estimated completion 2026-07: MAY CLOSE IMMINENTLY, re-check due. The de-escalation question asked properly (a 606-dermatologist survey shows the equipoise exists - secondhand)

5-FU + calcipotriene (1:1, 7-14 days) vs standard 5-FU x28 days for superficial BCC and SCC-in-situ (NCT05381597, Boston University): randomized single-blind pilot n=200, 3-year follow-up - RECRUITING, WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08-20 (last registry verification 2025-10 per search result), re-check due. The short-course de-escalation door on the low-risk menu
